description: M2 Source ingestion / Discover (tasks.md T2.1-T2.6, FR-1-FR-7, E-11, E-14). Add the SourceAdapter + HttpFetcher interfaces, an offline FixtureFetcher, the three source adapters (AnchorLink, GoogleCalendar, OfficialPage) plus a fixture source adapter, and a factory that wires fixture sources by default so the app runs offline. Depends on FEAT-001 only for shared models (SourceRecord already in M0 models). Produces SourceRecords consumed by later FEATs.
steps: Create vandy_food_radar/sources/__init__.py and vandy_food_radar/sources/base.py: define HttpFetcher Protocol (get(url: str, *, timeout: float) -> FetchResult where FetchResult carries status, body/text, and an optional error) and SourceAdapter Protocol (fetch(window) -> list[SourceRecord]). Add a small Window dataclass (target date) derived from config.target_window/timezone.

Create vandy_food_radar/sources/fixture_fetcher.py: FixtureFetcher implementing HttpFetcher by mapping a source_url to the fixture payload using vandy_food_radar.fixtures.load_all_json_fixtures() and load_text_fixture(); an unknown URL returns a FetchResult marked as a fetch error. This is the injected default when config.offline is True.

Create the adapters, each reading through the injected fetcher and emitting SourceRecord objects (id, event_id placeholder, source_id, source_url, raw_payload, parsed_fields, checked_at, source_updated_at, parse_status): vandy_food_radar/sources/anchor_link.py (AnchorLinkAdapter, keep only records whose raw perks include 'Free Food'), vandy_food_radar/sources/google_calendar.py (GoogleCalendarAdapter, incl. the calendar-only event E-14), vandy_food_radar/sources/official_page.py (OfficialPageFetcher used later by verify). Parse ISO timestamps into datetimes for checked_at/source_updated_at. A record with parse_status parse_error/fetch_error is surfaced with empty parsed_fields and never raises out of the adapter (FR-7, E-11).

Create vandy_food_radar/sources/factory.py with build_sources(config, fetcher) returning the enabled adapters, and a FixtureSourceAdapter that yields every corpus record; when config.offline, wire the FixtureFetcher so no network is touched.

Create tests/test_sources.py: each adapter returns expected records from fixtures with correct source_id and parse_status; the AnchorLink adapter applies the Free Food perk filter; the unparseable official page yields parse_status parse_error without raising; the calendar-only event is produced from the calendar source alone.
acceptance_criteria: SourceAdapter and HttpFetcher interfaces exist and adapters are constructor-injected with a fetcher (T2.1, FR-4).
AnchorLinkAdapter filters the Free Food perk; each adapter returns raw payload + parsed view + checked_at + parse_status (T2.2-T2.4, FR-1/2/3/5).
A fetch/parse error is recorded as parse_status and the run continues without an exception (T2.5, FR-7, AC-9 seam, E-11).
FixtureFetcher + factory let the corpus be ingested with no live network (offline default).
uv run pytest tests/test_sources.py passes and `make check` is green.
findings:
Implemented in vandy_food_radar/sources/ (base.py, fixture_fetcher.py, _common.py, anchor_link.py, google_calendar.py, official_page.py, factory.py, __init__.py). Import surface: `from vandy_food_radar.sources import build_sources, default_fetcher, FixtureFetcher, FixtureSourceAdapter, AnchorLinkAdapter, GoogleCalendarAdapter, OfficialPageAdapter, HttpFetcher, SourceAdapter, Window, FetchResult, fetch_official_page, official_page_records`.

INTERFACES (base.py):
- HttpFetcher Protocol: get(url: str, *, timeout: float = 10.0) -> FetchResult. NEVER raises.
- FetchResult dataclass: url, ok: bool, status: int|None, text: str|None, error: str|None. ok=True only when retrieved; on failure text=None and error is set.
- SourceAdapter Protocol: class attr `source_id: str`, method fetch(window: Window) -> list[SourceRecord]. NOTE: adapter.source_id is the STRING enum value (SourceId.X.value), NOT the SourceId enum; but each emitted SourceRecord.source_id IS the SourceId enum member. FixtureSourceAdapter.source_id == 'fixture'.
- Window dataclass: target_date: date. Build with Window.from_config(config, today=<date>) -> respects config.target_window (NEXT_DAY default => today+1; TODAY => today). `today` is injected, never read from clock (stays pure/testable). Fixture events are dated 2025-03-11, so the seed/pipeline step (FEAT-005+) must retarget dates onto the real window or get_events_for_day() will be empty.

SOURCERECORD WIRING (what build_source_record in _common.py produces per fixture record):
- id = 'src-'+uuid4hex (unique per call; adapters do NOT assign a stable id).
- event_id = '' (UNASSIGNED_EVENT_ID constant) -- placeholder; dedup/normalize (FEAT-003) must assign the canonical event id before persisting via Repository.save_event.
- source_id = SourceId enum member.
- source_url from fixture top-level source_url.
- raw_payload: TEXT. For JSON fixtures whose raw_payload is a dict, it is json.dumps(raw_payload, sort_keys=True) (the INNER payload only, e.g. anchor_link's {id,name,perks,...}); for HTML/official pages it is the verbatim HTML text; on fetch_error it holds the error string.
- parsed_fields: the fixture's parsed_fields dict when parse_status==OK, else {} (empty on parse_error/fetch_error).
- checked_at / source_updated_at: parsed from ISO8601 via datetime.fromisoformat (tz-aware); malformed/missing -> None (parse_iso_datetime never raises).
- parse_status: ParseStatus enum. Taken from the fixture's declared parse_status (unparseable_official_page.json => PARSE_ERROR); unknown URL / not-ok fetch => FETCH_ERROR. Errors are RETURNED as records, never raised (FR-7, E-11).

ADAPTERS:
- Each adapter is constructor-injected with an HttpFetcher: AnchorLinkAdapter(fetcher), GoogleCalendarAdapter(fetcher), OfficialPageAdapter(fetcher). They enumerate corpus records via _common.corpus_records_for(SourceId) (sorted by source_url) and fetch each source_url through the injected fetcher (honors the network seam even offline).
- AnchorLinkAdapter applies the Free Food perk filter: an OK record is kept only if its raw_payload JSON has perks list containing 'Free Food' (FREE_FOOD_PERK). Non-OK records are passed through unfiltered so failures stay visible.
- OfficialPageAdapter also exposes module helpers for the verify stage (FEAT-004): fetch_official_page(record: dict, fetcher) -> SourceRecord (single-URL, on-demand cross-check) and official_page_records() -> list[dict] (raw corpus official-page descriptors). Verify should reuse these instead of re-reading fixtures.

FIXTUREFETCHER (offline default): FixtureFetcher() loads load_all_json_fixtures() once and indexes by source_url. get(known_url) -> ok=200 with text = raw HTML (when fixture has raw_payload_file) else json.dumps(fixture_record, sort_keys=True). get(unknown_url) -> ok=False, status=404, error set. Note the returned text for a JSON fixture is the FULL fixture record (has top-level parse_status + parsed_fields), which build_source_record decodes; for HTML pages the body is HTML and build falls back to the corpus record's declared parse_status.

FACTORY: default_fetcher(config) -> FixtureFetcher (MVP has no live fetcher yet; online config also returns FixtureFetcher for now). build_sources(config, fetcher) -> list[SourceAdapter] honoring config.sources.<x>.enabled flags (all True by default). FixtureSourceAdapter(fetcher) yields one SourceRecord per JSON fixture across all three sources (whole corpus, unfiltered) for demos/e2e.

All modules: from __future__ import annotations, full annotations (mypy --strict clean), ruff+black clean. tests/test_sources.py green; full `make check` green (41 tests).
